name: Hu Ling-neng
bio: Hu Lingneng (胡令能, AD 785–826) was a mid-Tang recluse from Putian in Fujian. He is said to have worked in his youth as a travelling tinker, mending and fitting metal, and was nicknamed 'Hu the Tinker' (胡釘鉸).

According to the anecdote preserved in the Yunxi youyi, a man appeared to him in a dream, cut open his belly and put a book inside, after which he could compose poems. Four poems survive in the Complete Tang Poems; the best known, 'A Child Fishing', is a standard school text in China.

poems.title: 喜韓少府見訪 (Xi Han shaofu jian fang)
poems.author: Hu Ling-neng
poems.text:
忽聞梅福來相訪，笑著荷衣出草堂。
兒童不慣見車馬，走入蘆花深處藏。

poems.title: 王昭君 (Wang Zhaojun)
poems.author: Hu Ling-neng
poems.text:
胡風似劔鎪人骨，漢月如鉤釣胃腸。
魂夢不知身在路，夜來猶自到昭陽。

poems.title: 小兒垂釣 (Xiao er chui diao)
poems.author: Hu Ling-neng
poems.text:
蓬頭稚子學垂綸，側坐莓苔草映身。
路人借問遙招手，怕得魚驚不應人。

poems.title: 詠繡障 (Yong xiu zhang)
poems.author: Hu Ling-neng
poems.text:
日暮堂前花蘂嬌，爭拈小筆上牀描。
繡成安向春園裏，引得黃鶯下柳條。
